title.text: The Little Cloud Who Wanted to Help

s1.text: High up in the sky, above a quiet valley, floats a little white cloud. His name is Plume. He is round, light and very soft, like a cotton pillow. Every day, Plume drifts along with the wind. He watches the houses, the rivers and the birds. And every day, he wonders: “Could I help someone too?”

s2.text: One afternoon, Plume arrives above a big field of flowers. There are poppies, daisies and buttercups. But all the flowers are hanging their heads. The ground is dry and cracked. It has not rained for a very long time. “We are so thirsty,” whispers a little daisy. Plume’s heart feels a soft little squeeze.

s3.text: Plume thinks very hard. He is full of water drops, round and fresh, that he was saving for his big journey. “If I give away my rain, I will become very small,” he thinks. Then he looks again at the flowers, so very tired. Plume smiles. “Never mind. They need it more than I do. I am going to help them.”

s4.text: Plume takes a deep breath and lets his rain go. Pitter, patter, pitter, patter. Soft little drops fall on the petals, on the leaves, on the roots. The earth drinks slowly. One by one, the flowers lift their heads and open up to the sky. The field smells lovely, like wet grass after a summer shower.

s5.text: Now Plume is tiny, very light, almost see-through. But he is not sad at all. The flowers sway and sing: “Thank you, little cloud!” The evening sun paints Plume pink and gold. And the wind whispers in his ear: “You are very small, Plume, but your heart is enormous.”

s6.text: Night falls over the valley. The flowers close their petals, like little hands folding together. Plume settles above the hill, right next to the moon. Little by little, other clouds come to snuggle up against him, and he grows round again. Plume yawns. The flowers yawn. And you too, gently close your eyes.

outro.text: Even when you are small, you can do a lot of good. Good night, little one. Sweet dreams.
